title: Doubling Bigger Numbers
objective: Double a two-digit number by doubling the tens and the ones separately, then recombining — connects this unit back to Unit 2.1's place value.
studentQuestion: Can you double the tens and the ones separately, and put them back together?
newIdea: Distributing doubling across place value — an early, concrete instance of the Distribute pattern, well before D5 formalizes it for multiplication generally.

teaching.see: 23 is 2 tens and 3 ones — can we double each part separately?
teaching.transform: 40 + 6 = 46 — same value as double 23, reached by doubling the parts and recombining.

examples.transfer: double 38 — doubling the ones (16) crosses a ten, foreshadowing regrouping.

mastery.evidence: Correctly doubles 2 two-digit numbers by doubling tens and ones separately and recombining.
